sourceStatus: Official AQA June 2023 Physics Paper 3 compulsory Section A question paper and final mark scheme checked. SOURCE-ONLY part references, not playable questions, worked solutions or encoded marking rubrics.
subject: Physics
paperTitle: Paper 3 Section A (compulsory practical and data analysis)
paper3Composition: For an 80-mark A-level Physics Paper 3, combine this compulsory 45-mark Section A with exactly ONE chosen 35-mark optional Section B (7408/3BA, 3BB, 3BC, 3BD or 3BE). Never add all five options.
markingCaveats: Official general instructions allow a correct numerical result without working in many cases, but 'show working', figure annotations, graph drawing and invalid physics require specific evidence.
01.3: mark-point dependency applies to explaining g from the selected x-axis gradient; alternative valid linearisation methods and ECF are listed.
01.4: accepted graph readings and two valid kinematics routes have conditional follow-through and rounding allowances; do not hard-code one final number.
01.6: graph annotation is essential; official scheme permits two alternative graphical/kinematic routes and restricts integer flash-interval shortcuts.
02.2: a list question; extra incorrect assertions can cancel correct claims; experiment-specific data logging benefits, not vague advantages, matter.
02.3: both circuits must be assessed with a calculated minimum and explicit comparison to observed data; a circuit label alone is insufficient.
02.4: individual data cells are independently marked, including error-carried-forward for power; overall significant-figure penalty capped.
02.5: actual plotted graph evidence is needed; axis labels, linear scale and plotted curve have separate criteria.
02.6: graph extrapolation/read-off evidence and a valid alternative figure-based method are allowed; one mark is independent of the other.
03.1: alternative coherent argument that a search coil CAN be used with changing flux can earn marks, not only the static-field conclusion.
03.3: two-reading angle uncertainty and ECF produce distinct partial-mark patterns; arithmetic-only keyword matching is insufficient.
03.4–03.5: accepted numerical intervals derive from supplied graph and require appropriate significant figures.
03.7: mark scheme lists four annotated potential criteria but explicitly caps this three-mark graph question at MAX 3; do not award four.
General Physics guidance: contradictions may negate list marks; unit/sf policies, valid alternative approaches and graph evidence must be assessed before awarding credit.
Exact specification subtopic codes and machine-readable per-part rubrics remain unverified; topic summaries are independent editorial metadata.
